title: docs(changeset): the 8415 body states the row-identity property, not a stale read-site count (#10196)
body:
Fixes #10196
Clause-②: no

Prose only: the body of `.changeset/8415-filter-builder-condition-id.md`. The front matter is byte-identical (`cmp` against base `f8a9d0fb0`, exit 0). No code or test changes.

## What was false

1. **The count sentence (the card's subject).** The body said `id` has **sixteen** condition-side read sites in three categories. At base `f8a9d0fb0` I count **17**, and the three categories do not cover all of them. objectui#10189 added a read that builds a DOM id. It is not a MATCH site, not the React `key`, and not a call site that passes the id to a mutator.
2. **The reported-location sentence (same file, same defect class, fixed here under the bounded in-place rule; see below).** The body said `safeValidateSchema` reports a single root `invalid_union` at `path: []` across **13** arms, with the `id` failure inside arm 8. That was true when objectui#8432 landed. objectui#8498 (squash `67749c724`) then made the document-level union discriminated on `type`, which made the claim false. Today the reported issue is a single `invalid_union` at `path: ["value"]`, and nothing wraps it at the root. The pending `8498-any-component-union-discriminated.md` body says the same thing: "rather than one `invalid_union` at the root with them nested inside". Both bodies publish into the same CHANGELOG, so they would have contradicted each other.

## Decision: state the property, not a count (card acceptance item 3)

I dropped the count. Nothing in the body's argument depends on how many reads there are. The argument depends on three things: every row mutator matches its row by `id`, the row `key` is `id`, and nothing matches a row by index. The file gained a read once already (objectui#10189), and that turned a true count into a false one. A re-derived "17" would go stale the same way on the next such PR. AGENTS.md #9 says the same: point at the instrument, do not write down its answer. The replacement states the property, names the four MATCH sites (the simulation later in the body transcribes those four helpers), and names the instrument that re-derives part of the property: the `re-derived from the reader` block of `packages/types/src/__tests__/filter-builder-condition-id-8415.test.ts`, which pins the four MATCH sites and `key={condition.id}` from the component source. It also says that nothing pins the other half ("every call hands it `condition.id`", "nothing matches a row by index").

## Changed sentences, before and after

**Paragraph 1: before**

> Re-derived from `packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx` rather than inherited: `id` has **sixteen** condition-side read sites — the four MATCH sites that decide which row a mutation lands on (`removeCondition`'s `c.id !== conditionId`, `updateCondition`'s and `changeOperator`'s `c.id === conditionId`, `changeField`'s `c.id !== conditionId`), the React `key` on the row, and eleven call sites that hand `condition.id` to one of those four.

**Paragraph 1: after**

> Re-derived from `packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx` rather than inherited, and stated as a property rather than as a tally of read sites, since that file keeps gaining `condition.id` reads and a count goes stale with the next one: **which row an edit lands on is decided by `id` and by nothing else.** Each mutator that acts on a single row picks it with a MATCH on `id` (`removeCondition`'s `c.id !== conditionId`, `updateCondition`'s and `changeOperator`'s `c.id === conditionId`, `changeField`'s `c.id !== conditionId`), every call to one of them hands it `condition.id`, the row's React `key` is `condition.id`, and nothing in the file matches a row by its index. The file's other reads of `condition.id` pick no row; one of them builds the element id that a half-filled range's blank bound names in `aria-describedby`. The MATCH sites and the `key` are re-derived from the component source by the `re-derived from the reader` block of `packages/types/src/__tests__/filter-builder-condition-id-8415.test.ts`; the rest of the property is read off the source, and no test pins it.

**Paragraph 2: before** (only the sentences that changed)

> The issue `safeValidateSchema` actually reports is a single root `invalid_union` at `path: []`, across **13** arms; the `id` failure sits three nested unions further down, inside arm 8: `invalid_union` at `["value"]` → arm 1 → `invalid_union` at `["conditions", 0]` → arm 0 → `invalid_type` at `["id"]`, *"Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"*.

**Paragraph 2: after**

> The issue `safeValidateSchema` actually reports is a single `invalid_union` at `path: ["value"]`. The document-level union is discriminated on `type` (objectui#8498), so it hands back the `filter-builder` schema's own issues instead of nesting them under a root union. The `id` failure sits inside two nested unions: that `invalid_union` → arm 1 (`FilterGroupSchema`) → `invalid_union` at `["conditions", 0]` → arm 0 (`FilterBuilderConditionSchema`) → `invalid_type` at `["id"]`, *"Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"*.

Nothing else in the body changed. I re-read every other sentence against `f8a9d0fb0`; see the Acceptance notes.

## Evidence

### Read sites, re-derived (not copied from the card)

The command is `grep -nE '\b(condition|c)\.id\b' packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx`, run at `f8a9d0fb0`. Current `main` (`923e1b8ab`) has an empty diff against it on this file and on the other measured files. I also ran the same pattern against the two trees the card names, as a control. It gives back the card's figures, so the instrument reproduces them:

| tree | hits |
|:--|--:|
| `e686f4d9a` (tree the claim was written against) | 16 |
| `befd40ccd` (card's `main`) | 17 |
| `f8a9d0fb0` (this branch's base) | 17 |

All 17 hits at `f8a9d0fb0`, classified:

- **MATCH site (4):** `:1213` `removeCondition` `c.id !== conditionId` · `:1228` `updateCondition` `c.id === conditionId` · `:1247` `changeOperator` `c.id === conditionId` · `:1307` `changeField` `c.id !== conditionId`
- **React key (1):** `:1752` `key={condition.id}`
- **Call site handing the id to a MATCH-site helper (11):** `updateCondition(condition.id, …)` at `:1396`, `:1429`, `:1453`, `:1478`, `:1554`, `:1618`, `:1657`, `:1705` · `changeField(condition.id, …)` at `:1757` · `changeOperator(condition.id, …)` at `:1781` · `removeCondition(condition.id)` at `:1808`
- **Other (1):** `:1531` `` const incompleteId = `filter-range-incomplete-${condition.id}` ``. This builds the `id` of the incomplete-range message element, and the blank bound names it in `aria-describedby` (objectui#10189).

4 + 1 + 11 + 1 = 17. Other spellings: every `.id` in the file outside these 17 is one hit, `r?.id` in the lookup-option mapper, which reads a referenced record and not a condition. Nothing reads `filterGroup.id`. Every call to the four mutators passes `condition.id`: `grep -cE '\b(updateCondition|changeField|changeOperator|removeCondition)\(condition\.id'` gives 11, and the unfiltered call list (comment lines excluded) also has 11 lines.

### Property check, both directions

- **By `id` (present):** the four MATCH sites above. `addCondition` appends and matches no row. `clearAllConditions` empties the list. `toggleLogic` edits the group.
- **By index (absent):** `findIndex` 0, `splice` 0, `indexOf` 0, `conditions[` 0. The row render is `filterGroup.conditions.map((condition) => …)`, with no index parameter. The only index-taking code in the file is **inside one condition's value**: `setBound(index: 0 | 1, …)` writes `next[index]` of a range's two-bound tuple, and the multi-value chip input's `removeAt(index)` / `values.map((v, index) => …)` works on one row's value list. Neither picks a row.

### Reported location, re-measured (probe via `tsx` against `packages/types/src`, at `f8a9d0fb0`)

```
== missing id: success=false
  invalid_union path=["value"] arms=2
    [arm 0] invalid_type ["field"] · invalid_value ["operator"]
    [arm 1] invalid_union path=["conditions",0] arms=2
        [arm 0] invalid_type path=["id"] "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"
== id: 42 → same place: [arm 1] → ["conditions",0] [arm 0] → invalid_type ["id"] "…received number"
== { logic: 'and', conditions: [] } (no group id): success=true
FilterBuilderConditionSchema.safeParse(no id) → flat invalid_type at ["id"]
```

Order: `git merge-base --is-ancestor a407bd654 67749c724` exits 0, meaning objectui#8432's squash is an ancestor of objectui#8498's. The reverse direction exits 1. As a control, `a407bd654` measured against `HEAD` exits 0. The checkout is not shallow (`--is-shallow-repository` is `false`). So the 13-arm reading predates the discrimination and went false when it landed.

### Why the second fix is in scope (bounded in-place rule: all four conditions hold)

1. Same defect class as the card: a pending changeset body publishes a measured claim, and a later PR made it false.
2. The fix is mechanical and the shape is already fixed by the card: prose only, front matter untouched, re-derived rather than copied, `check-changeset-overwrite` case 2.
3. No other claim holds the file. The claim's file surface is this file, body only.
4. It is checked by the same gate family, with no new verification surface.

The dispatch put "any sentence the re-derivation makes false" in scope for this file. This sentence was made false by a different change. I fixed it here, and I am saying so here, instead of letting it publish.

## Gates, at head `0df5f7ce3`

| gate | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0: "No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed." |
| `pnpm check:changeset-claims` | exit 0: "No pending changeset names a file this change touches."; polarity pass over the 1 modified body |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` | exit 0 (report-only): `M .changeset/8415-filter-builder-condition-id.md`, "declared at base: @object-ui/types: minor", "declares now: @object-ui/types: minor". This is case 2, a deliberate correction. |
| `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` | exit 0: "No test source names a pending changeset." |
| `pnpm changeset:check` | exit 0: fixed group ok; "No changeset declares a `major` bump." |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | exit 0: "check-control-bytes: OK" |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | exit 0: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)` |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test .changeset/8415-filter-builder-condition-id.md` | exit 0: "NOT GOVERNED" |
| front matter `cmp` against base | exit 0 (34 bytes, identical) |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/filter-builder-condition-id-8415.test.ts`, the test the new text cites | `Tests 12 passed (12)`, run under the shared verify lock |

No type-check or unit-test run is owed for a prose-only change. I ran the one test because the new sentence cites it as a live instrument.

## Acceptance notes

- **Other counts in the same body, re-read and left alone:** "7 of 7, across the three schema-catalog entries". Re-measured at `f8a9d0fb0`, it is still 7 of 7 across `product-search` (3), `search-interface` (2) and `with-conditions` (2), and `packages/components/docs/FilterBuilder.md` also carries `id: 'cond-1'`. It is true, it is framed as a measurement, and the card did not ask for it, so I left it. It is the same half-life shape, though.
- **"The renderer is unchanged; `FilterOperatorSchema`, `FilterFieldSchema` and `FilterBuilderSchema`'s own keys are byte-identical"** describes objectui#8432's own diff, not the tree. Read that way it is still true, so I left it, even though the sibling `6939-filter-builder-mirror.md` in the same release does change `FilterFieldSchema`.
- **Still true against `f8a9d0fb0`:** the compile-time-face paragraph (the TS `FilterBuilderCondition.id` is required, `FilterGroup.id` is optional, and `complex.ts` has not changed these since `a407bd654`), the simulation bullets (the four helper bodies are unchanged in shape), `addCondition` emitting `crypto.randomUUID()`, and "nothing reads `filterGroup.id`".
- **Why no gate caught sentence 2:** the `changeset-claim-re-read` gate only resolves backticked **file names**. objectui#8498 edited `packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts`, and the 8415 body names the behaviour through the symbol `safeValidateSchema`. The gate's own text lists "a claim spelled as a symbol … rather than a backticked file name" as not covered, so this is a declared boundary, not a new gap.
- **Sibling changesets not touched**, as the card directs: `6939-filter-builder-mirror.md`, `6515-record-form-current-user-normaliser.md`, `6559-expression-user-input-contract.md`, `palette-canonical-discussion-5495.md`.
- **Unmeasured observation, not filed:** `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx` builds condition ids from positions (`` id: `c${i}` ``) when it hands rules to the FilterBuilder. The builder itself matches by `id`, which is what this body claims. Whether renumbering after a remove moves any per-row UI state was not measured. Carrier: none.

Dispatched by the PM loop (`domain:ui` seat 1). Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`.
